items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine

ctx.x: Well this is sort of a two part question. I wonder if you had definite goals for a life in music and did your mother support them? Did she think you were going into the right career?

Well it started like I never had goals. I never had goals. And I’ve been blessed things fell in my lap. I never would have auditioned with Benny Goodman, he called me. I never auditioned with Woody Herman, he called me. I never auditioned with Steve Allen, Regis Philbin, they called me. So I’ve been blessed in that way, and I never had goals. I wanted to play good. That was my goal if anything, I just wanted to play to where I enjoyed it. I never, you know it’s wild to say I never play for an audience. I play for…
Okay yes that’s — I’m going to catch a plan out there and get that.

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: I have a feeling you still have to get the last word in.

No, no. Only from the band. You know something? When I worked with Steve Allen for years, conducting, my job was to conduct. There’s a director and a producer. Whatever they have to tell me. But if it comes to my department, they hire me to do the job, I’ll tell them. Otherwise don’t give me that job. And I’ll take a lot of advice of musicians. The thing is, but I don’t do record — when I first moved to California I’d go to do a record date and there’d be some idiot up there and we’d be doing 84 takes and I’d…

good arrangers, and sometimes when it came to the rock era, there’d be no music, they didn’t even know what they’re doing. You get a lead sheet, and you have to make up your own part half the time. But then again you’d stay there hours because it’s an E flat chord. If he would just say “E flat” and we all played it, that would solve the whole problem. But he’d mention everything but E flat. And the guys loved it because they’d go home with a lot of money. And that wasn’t for me. The music has always been the most…
